customManagers.description: Swift releases. swiftlang/swift tags them swift-X.Y.Z-RELEASE. Version and commit are captured by ONE regex so Renovate moves them together -- build.sh fetches SWIFT_TAG with clone_pinned.sh, which fails unless the checkout is exactly SWIFT_SHA, so a version bumped without its commit fails closed.

The swiftlang/llvm-project commit the build support is cut from. llvm-project tags every Swift release swift-X.Y.Z-RELEASE, exactly as swiftlang/swift does, so this tracks that tag the same way: version and commit in ONE regex. The version is LLVM_SWIFT_RELEASE rather than SWIFT_VERSION only because two managers capturing the same literal would both rewrite it; build-llvm.sh fails unless the two are equal and LLVM_SHA is the commit at the tag.

swift-cmark, the compiler's Markdown parser, tagged swift-X.Y.Z-RELEASE per Swift release like llvm-project and tracked the same way: version and commit in ONE regex. build-toolchain.sh runs check_release_pin on it.

mavericks-clang-22's cross toolchain, the C/C++ compiler of the 10.9-hosted Swift toolchain. The whole pin is the version: fetch-clang22.sh verifies the pkg against that release's own SHA256SUMS. The versioning regex reads -mavericks.N as the build number; Renovate's default would coerce it away and never propose a repackage.

packageRules.description: ONE PR per Swift release, moving the Swift pin, the llvm-project pin and the swift-cmark pin together. Apart, each fails its release-pin check (build-llvm.sh, build-toolchain.sh), so none could merge.

EXCEPTION to the family ship-if-green default. A MINOR or MAJOR Swift bump is held: the runtime patches are cut against specific stdlib and runtime internals, so a bump that happens to build proves nothing about the 10.9 behaviour a macOS 26 runner cannot see. Needs a human until CI can run the real-10.9 gate (umbrella track E, vm-guest). A PATCH bump takes the family default.
